# Copilot Instructions

## Accessibility
- Build accessible interaction patterns by default: prefer semantic HTML and native controls, provide programmatic labels and instructions, support keyboard operation, preserve visible focus, and announce asynchronous status or errors when useful.
- Do not communicate meaning, state, or action through color alone. Pair color with text, shape, patterns, icons, or other redundant cues; ensure charts and visual summaries have text alternatives.
- Choose palettes with distinguishable colors and sufficient contrast in both light and dark themes. Verify accessible behavior with focused tests when changing UI.

## Protected About Section
- Do not edit the About section unless the user explicitly directs you to do so. This includes its component, content, structure, styles, and About-specific tests or assertions.
